# PROJECT: AI-POWERED CAREER AND CONSULTATION PLATFORM

Act as a senior full-stack software engineer, system architect, backend engineer, frontend engineer, database designer, AI engineer, and QA engineer.

Your task is to BUILD a complete, functional, production-oriented web application that satisfies all the requirements described below.

Do not create only a prototype, static UI, or frontend demonstration. Implement a working full-stack application with frontend, backend, database integration, AI functionality, payment integration, calendar integration, email notifications, validation, testing, and documentation.

Work directly inside the project workspace. Create the required files, implement the code, run the application, execute tests, diagnose errors, and fix them.

Do not stop after producing an architecture diagram or project plan. Continue implementing the application until the requirements have been addressed.

==================================================
1. PROJECT OBJECTIVE
==================================================

Build an AI-powered career platform where users can:

1. Register and log in securely.
2. Manage their personal profiles.
3. Chat with an AI career assistant.
4. Create and manage multiple AI chat sessions.
5. Generate professional resumes using AI.
6. Edit resumes using Tiptap.
7. Choose between two resume templates.
8. Preview and export resumes.
9. Book consultations with career experts.
10. Pay for consultations through Stripe.
11. Receive Google Calendar meeting links.
12. Receive confirmation emails.
13. View application statistics on a dashboard.
14. Manage their resumes, conversations, and consultations.

The application must be responsive, accessible, secure, modular, maintainable, and easy to run locally.

==================================================
2. TECHNOLOGY STACK
==================================================

Use the following technologies.

FRONTEND:
- Next.js with the App Router.
- React.
- TypeScript.
- Tailwind CSS.
- A consistent reusable component system.
- Tiptap for rich-text resume editing.
- React Hook Form and Zod, where appropriate, for form validation.
- A suitable charting library only if dashboard charts are useful.

BACKEND:
- Node.js.
- Express.js.
- TypeScript.
- REST APIs.
- Mongoose.
- Zod or an equivalent validation library.
- Centralized error-handling middleware.
- Structured logging.

DATABASE:
- MongoDB.
- Well-designed schemas.
- Appropriate references and embedded documents.
- Validation.
- Unique constraints.
- Indexes for common queries.

AI:
- A configurable LLM provider.
- A backend-only AI integration layer.
- Structured AI-generated resume content.
- Persistent chat history.
- Configurable model and provider settings.

INTEGRATIONS:
- Stripe for payments.
- Stripe webhooks for payment confirmation.
- Google Calendar API for meeting creation.
- Nodemailer or another configurable email provider.
- Swagger/OpenAPI for API documentation.

TESTING:
- Jest or Vitest as appropriate.
- Supertest for backend API tests.
- React Testing Library where useful.
- Playwright for end-to-end testing if time permits.

DEVELOPMENT:
- Git.
- GitHub-ready repository.
- Docker Compose if practical.
- Environment-variable configuration.
- ESLint and Prettier.

Use compatible, stable package versions. Inspect the installed Node.js and package-manager versions before choosing dependencies.

Do not use deprecated packages unnecessarily.

==================================================
3. ARCHITECTURE
==================================================

Implement a modular microservice-oriented architecture.

For the initial implementation, use a modular monolith if independently deployed microservices would create unnecessary complexity. Maintain clear module boundaries so the modules can be extracted into separate services later.

Separate the system into these modules:

1. Authentication and User Management.
2. AI Career Assistant.
3. Resume Management.
4. AI Resume Generation.
5. Consultant Management.
6. Consultation Booking.
7. Payment Management.
8. Google Calendar Integration.
9. Email Notification.
10. Dashboard and Analytics.

The architecture should follow this general flow:

Next.js Frontend
       |
       v
Backend API Layer
       |
       +---- Authentication Module
       |
       +---- User Module
       |
       +---- AI Chat Module
       |
       +---- Resume Module
       |
       +---- Booking Module
       |
       +---- Payment Module
       |
       +---- Calendar Integration
       |
       +---- Email Integration
       |
       +---- Dashboard Module
                    |
                    v
                 MongoDB

External integrations:

AI Module --------> LLM Provider
Payment Module ---> Stripe
Calendar Module --> Google Calendar API
Email Module -----> Email Provider

Create an architecture diagram and document the design decisions.

Avoid creating unnecessary services, abstractions, or infrastructure that do not improve the application.

==================================================
4. PROJECT STRUCTURE
==================================================

Organize the codebase clearly.

Use a structure similar to:

career-platform/
|
|-- frontend/
|   |-- app/
|   |-- components/
|   |-- features/
|   |-- hooks/
|   |-- lib/
|   |-- services/
|   |-- types/
|   |-- public/
|   |-- tests/
|   |-- package.json
|
|-- backend/
|   |-- src/
|   |   |-- config/
|   |   |-- middleware/
|   |   |-- modules/
|   |   |   |-- auth/
|   |   |   |-- users/
|   |   |   |-- chat/
|   |   |   |-- resumes/
|   |   |   |-- consultants/
|   |   |   |-- bookings/
|   |   |   |-- payments/
|   |   |   |-- calendar/
|   |   |   |-- notifications/
|   |   |   |-- dashboard/
|   |   |-- integrations/
|   |   |-- utils/
|   |   |-- app.ts
|   |   |-- server.ts
|   |-- tests/
|   |-- package.json
|
|-- docs/
|   |-- architecture.md
|   |-- database-design.md
|   |-- api-documentation.md
|   |-- testing.md
|
|-- docker-compose.yml
|-- .gitignore
|-- .env.example
|-- README.md

You may adjust the structure when justified, but keep the frontend and backend responsibilities clearly separated.

==================================================
5. UI/UX DESIGN
==================================================

Build a polished, modern, professional SaaS interface.

Use a consistent design system throughout the application.

Design direction:
- Clean professional layout.
- Neutral background colors.
- Consistent typography.
- Clear spacing.
- Well-designed cards.
- Subtle borders and shadows.
- Accessible contrast.
- Responsive navigation.
- Mobile-friendly layouts.
- Loading skeletons.
- Empty states.
- Error states.
- Success notifications.
- Confirmation dialogs for destructive operations.
- Accessible form controls.

Create a sidebar-based dashboard layout for authenticated users.

Sidebar navigation:
- Dashboard.
- AI Career Assistant.
- My Resumes.
- Create Resume.
- Consultations.
- Profile.
- Logout.

The public-facing pages should include:
- Landing page.
- Registration.
- Login.

Use reusable components for buttons, cards, forms, modals, navigation, notifications, loading states, and error displays.

Do not prioritize decorative animations over functionality.

All buttons and interactive elements must perform their intended actions. Do not leave fake buttons, dead links, or nonfunctional forms.

==================================================
6. AUTHENTICATION AND USER MANAGEMENT
==================================================

Implement:

- User registration.
- User login.
- Logout.
- Secure password hashing using Argon2id or bcrypt.
- Authentication middleware.
- Protected frontend pages.
- Protected backend APIs.
- User profile retrieval.
- User profile updating.
- Input validation.
- Appropriate error responses.

Use secure session or token-based authentication.

Prefer secure, HTTP-only cookies with an appropriate session or access-token strategy. Protect state-changing requests against CSRF when required by the chosen authentication design.

Do not store passwords in plain text.

Do not place sensitive tokens in localStorage.

Implement authorization checks so users can access only their own private data.

Create the following user roles:

- USER
- ADMIN
- CONSULTANT

Implement role-based access control where necessary.

Optional if time permits:
- Email verification.
- Password reset.
- Refresh-token rotation.

Do not implement authentication merely by hiding frontend pages. Enforce authentication and authorization on the backend.

==================================================
7. USER PROFILE
==================================================

Create a profile page where users can manage:

- Full name.
- Email.
- Phone number.
- Professional headline.
- Biography.
- Education.
- Skills.
- Work experience.
- Projects.
- Certifications.

Validate all inputs.

Keep profile data separate from authentication credentials.

Provide APIs to retrieve and update the authenticated user's profile.

==================================================
8. AI CAREER ASSISTANT
==================================================

Build a ChatGPT-like career assistant.

Required features:

- Create a new chat session.
- Rename a chat session.
- Send a message.
- Receive an AI response.
- Save user messages.
- Save AI messages.
- Display previous conversations.
- Reopen existing conversations.
- Continue existing conversations.
- Delete a conversation.
- Maintain conversation context.
- Display loading and error states.
- Prevent unauthorized access to conversations.

Create MongoDB models for ChatSession and ChatMessage.

Suggested fields:

ChatSession:
- userId.
- title.
- createdAt.
- updatedAt.

ChatMessage:
- sessionId.
- role.
- content.
- createdAt.

Add indexes for common session and message queries.

AI request workflow:

1. Authenticate the user.
2. Validate the request.
3. Verify ownership of the chat session.
4. Load relevant conversation history.
5. Construct the LLM request.
6. Call the configured AI provider.
7. Handle provider errors and timeouts.
8. Save the user message and assistant response.
9. Return the response to the frontend.

Keep API keys exclusively on the backend.

Use environment variables to configure the AI provider and model.

Do not hardcode an API key.

Create a provider abstraction so that the LLM provider can be changed without rewriting the chat application.

If credentials are missing, show a clear setup message and provide a mock provider for local UI development and automated tests.

The mock provider must be clearly identified as a development fallback. Never present mock responses as real AI-generated results.

Implement:
- Rate limiting.
- Request timeouts.
- Error handling.
- Reasonable message-length limits.

Streaming responses and token tracking are optional enhancements.

==================================================
9. AI RESUME BUILDER
==================================================

Build a complete resume creation workflow.

Users must be able to:

- Create a resume.
- Enter structured resume data.
- Generate resume content with AI.
- Edit the generated content.
- Save changes.
- Reload saved resumes.
- View a list of their resumes.
- Update resumes.
- Delete resumes.
- Duplicate resumes if time permits.
- Preview resumes.
- Select a resume template.
- Export the resume as a downloadable document.

Required resume sections:

1. Personal Information.
2. Professional Summary.
3. Education.
4. Experience.
5. Skills.
6. Projects.
7. Certifications.
8. Achievements.

Use a structured MongoDB resume model.

Do not use raw HTML as the only stored representation of a resume.

Store resume content independently of the presentation template.

Each resume should belong to an authenticated user.

Validate the resume structure on the backend.

The AI generation workflow must use information provided by the user.

Do not invent employment history, degrees, certifications, awards, or other credentials.

If required information is missing, ask the user to provide it or leave the relevant section empty.

Allow users to regenerate specific sections without unnecessarily overwriting the rest of the resume.

==================================================
10. RESUME TEMPLATES
==================================================

Implement at least two templates.

TEMPLATE A: MODERN PROFESSIONAL

Design characteristics:
- Modern typography.
- Clear visual hierarchy.
- Balanced whitespace.
- Attractive professional layout.
- Readable section headings.

TEMPLATE B: ATS CLASSIC

Design characteristics:
- Simple, conventional layout.
- Standard section headings.
- Minimal graphics.
- Single-column layout where practical.
- Consistent formatting.
- Machine-readable text.

Both templates must consume the same structured resume data.

Switching templates must not duplicate or destroy the resume content.

Create a template-selection interface with live previews.

==================================================
11. TIPTAP RESUME EDITOR
==================================================

Integrate Tiptap.

Users must be able to:

- Edit resume content.
- Format text.
- Edit section content.
- Save changes.
- Reload saved changes.
- Preview the result.
- Apply a selected template.

Implement reliable synchronization between the structured resume data and the editor.

Avoid accidental data loss when switching templates or navigating away.

Autosave and resume version history are optional enhancements.

Sanitize or safely render user-editable content. Do not expose the application to stored cross-site scripting vulnerabilities.

==================================================
12. ATS-FRIENDLY OUTPUT
==================================================

Use semantic HTML.

Use appropriate heading hierarchy.

Ensure resume content is machine-readable text.

Avoid rendering the entire resume as an image.

Keep section structures clear and consistent.

Minimize unnecessary graphics and decorative elements in the ATS Classic template.

Implement an export feature that produces a useful resume document.

Test the exported output for:
- Missing text.
- Broken page layout.
- Incorrect section order.
- Unexpected empty sections.
- Readability.

Document the ATS-friendly design decisions in the README.

Do not claim universal compatibility with all ATS software.

==================================================
13. CONSULTANT MANAGEMENT
==================================================

Create a consultant model.

Store relevant information such as:

- Name.
- Professional title.
- Biography.
- Areas of expertise.
- Email or contact information where appropriate.
- Consultation duration.
- Consultation price.
- Availability.
- Active/inactive status.

Create a consultant listing page.

Display consultant information and available appointment slots.

Create an admin or consultant-facing mechanism for managing availability if practical.

Seed a few clearly identified demonstration consultants for local development.

Do not hardcode fake consultant data into production request handlers.

==================================================
14. CONSULTATION BOOKING
==================================================

Implement consultation booking.

Booking form fields:

- Consultant.
- Date.
- Start time.
- End time or consultation duration.
- User name.
- Email.
- Phone.
- Meeting agenda.

Business rules:

1. Reject bookings in the past.
2. Validate consultant availability.
3. Validate time-slot boundaries.
4. Prevent overlapping bookings.
5. Prevent concurrent requests from double-booking the same slot.
6. Persist booking status.
7. Persist payment status.
8. Restrict access to private booking details.
9. Validate cancellation and rescheduling rules if implemented.

Use a consistent time-zone strategy. Store timestamps consistently and display times in the intended user's or consultant's time zone.

Implement backend validation even if the frontend already validates the form.

Create database constraints or a suitable reservation strategy to protect against concurrent booking attempts.

Use appropriate database transactions when supported and configured.

Do not assume that a frontend availability check guarantees the slot remains available.

==================================================
15. BOOKING STATE MANAGEMENT
==================================================

Implement an explicit booking state machine.

Suggested states:

- PENDING_PAYMENT.
- PAYMENT_FAILED.
- PAID.
- CONFIRMED.
- CANCELLED.
- COMPLETED.

Define valid transitions.

Reject invalid state transitions.

Keep booking status separate from payment status.

A successful payment must not be incorrectly marked as failed because a later calendar or email integration fails.

Record integration failures and provide retry mechanisms.

==================================================
16. STRIPE PAYMENT INTEGRATION
==================================================

Integrate Stripe Checkout or another appropriate Stripe payment flow.

Use Stripe test mode during development.

Payment workflow:

1. User selects an available consultation.
2. Backend validates availability and creates a pending booking.
3. Backend creates a payment session.
4. Frontend redirects the user to the Stripe payment page.
5. User completes payment.
6. Stripe sends a webhook to the backend.
7. Backend verifies the webhook signature.
8. Backend processes the payment event idempotently.
9. Backend updates the payment record.
10. Backend transitions the booking to the appropriate state.
11. Backend triggers calendar and email workflows.

Important security requirements:

- Use backend-calculated prices.
- Never trust prices supplied by the browser.
- Verify webhook signatures.
- Keep Stripe secret keys on the backend.
- Handle duplicate webhook delivery.
- Store processed event identifiers.
- Avoid duplicate booking confirmation.
- Handle payment failure and cancellation.
- Use appropriate idempotency strategies.

The frontend success redirect must not be treated as authoritative payment confirmation.

Create a Payment model containing relevant information such as:

- Booking ID.
- User ID.
- Stripe session ID.
- Stripe payment intent ID where applicable.
- Amount.
- Currency.
- Payment status.
- Processed event identifiers or references.
- Timestamps.

Never store raw payment-card details.

Create clear setup instructions for Stripe test credentials and webhook testing.

==================================================
17. GOOGLE CALENDAR INTEGRATION
==================================================

After successful payment and booking confirmation, create a Google Calendar event for the consultation.

Persist:
- External event ID.
- Meeting URL where available.
- Event start time.
- Event end time.
- Calendar integration status.

Handle API failures gracefully.

If payment succeeds but calendar creation fails:
- Preserve the successful payment.
- Preserve the booking record.
- Record the calendar failure.
- Make the calendar operation retryable.
- Avoid creating duplicate calendar events during retries.

Use environment variables for credentials and follow the selected Google authentication approach.

Document the required Google Cloud setup.

If credentials are not configured, allow local development and automated tests to use a clearly identified mock calendar adapter.

Do not falsely claim that a real Google Calendar event was created when the mock adapter was used.

==================================================
18. EMAIL NOTIFICATIONS
==================================================

Send a confirmation email after successful payment and booking confirmation.

Include:
- User name.
- Consultant name.
- Consultation date.
- Consultation time.
- Meeting URL where available.
- Booking ID.

Use a configurable email provider.

Store relevant notification status and error details where useful.

Handle temporary provider failures with retryable operations.

Avoid sending duplicate emails when webhook events are delivered multiple times.

Provide a mock email adapter for local development and tests if credentials are unavailable.

Clearly document how to configure the real email provider.

==================================================
19. MONGODB DATABASE DESIGN
==================================================

Create appropriate Mongoose models for:

- User.
- ChatSession.
- ChatMessage.
- Resume.
- Consultant.
- Booking.
- Payment.
- Calendar integration details or equivalent persisted metadata.
- Notification delivery records if useful.

For every model:
- Define field types.
- Add required-field validation.
- Define relationships.
- Add timestamps.
- Create appropriate indexes.
- Enforce unique constraints where required.
- Consider expected query patterns.

Use references for entities with independent lifecycles.

Embed related information when it is naturally owned by a single document and benefits from being retrieved together.

Create a database-design document that explains the schema decisions.

Ensure all user-owned records are scoped to the authenticated user.

Do not rely on frontend filtering for data isolation.

==================================================
20. DASHBOARD AND ANALYTICS
==================================================

Implement a dashboard API.

Example:

GET /api/dashboard

Example response:

{
  "totalResumes": 5,
  "totalChats": 23,
  "upcomingConsultations": 2,
  "completedConsultations": 7
}

Calculate these values using real database data.

Display them in the frontend dashboard.

Include:
- Total resumes.
- Total chat sessions.
- Upcoming consultations.
- Completed consultations.

Handle users with no data.

Use efficient database queries or aggregation pipelines.

Ensure the API returns statistics only for the authenticated user.

Document the relevant indexes and query decisions.

==================================================
21. SERVER-SIDE PAGINATION, SEARCH, SORTING, FILTERING
==================================================

At least one major listing API must support all of the following on the backend:

- Pagination.
- Search.
- Sorting.
- Filtering.

Prefer the bookings listing API.

Example:

GET /api/bookings?page=1&limit=10&status=CONFIRMED&search=rahul&sort=-createdAt

Validate query parameters.

Enforce reasonable pagination limits.

Whitelist allowed sorting fields.

Apply filters in MongoDB.

Return pagination metadata.

Example response:

{
  "data": [],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 1,
    "limit": 10,
    "total": 0,
    "totalPages": 0
  }
}

Do not fetch all records and perform pagination only in the frontend.

==================================================
22. API DESIGN
==================================================

Use consistent REST API conventions.

Suggested endpoints include:

AUTH:
- POST /api/auth/register
- POST /api/auth/login
- POST /api/auth/logout

USER:
- GET /api/users/me
- PATCH /api/users/me

CHAT:
- POST /api/chat/sessions
- GET /api/chat/sessions
- GET /api/chat/sessions/:sessionId
- PATCH /api/chat/sessions/:sessionId
- DELETE /api/chat/sessions/:sessionId
- POST /api/chat/sessions/:sessionId/messages

RESUMES:
- POST /api/resumes
- GET /api/resumes
- GET /api/resumes/:id
- PATCH /api/resumes/:id
- DELETE /api/resumes/:id
- POST /api/resumes/:id/generate
- POST /api/resumes/:id/export

CONSULTANTS:
- GET /api/consultants
- GET /api/consultants/:id
- GET /api/consultants/:id/availability

BOOKINGS:
- POST /api/bookings
- GET /api/bookings
- GET /api/bookings/:id
- PATCH /api/bookings/:id/cancel

PAYMENTS:
- POST /api/payments/checkout
- POST /api/payments/webhook

DASHBOARD:
- GET /api/dashboard

Adjust endpoints when appropriate.

Do not create multiple endpoints that duplicate the same functionality without a clear reason.

Document:
- HTTP method.
- URL.
- Authentication requirements.
- Request schema.
- Response schema.
- HTTP status codes.
- Error responses.

Generate Swagger/OpenAPI documentation.

Use appropriate status codes and a consistent error-response structure.

==================================================
23. SECURITY
==================================================

Implement:

- Server-side input validation.
- Authentication middleware.
- Resource ownership checks.
- Role-based authorization.
- Secure password hashing.
- Appropriate CORS configuration.
- Rate limiting.
- Request-size limits.
- Secure cookie settings where applicable.
- Environment-variable secrets.
- Safe error responses.
- Protection against NoSQL injection.
- Safe rendering of editable content.
- Stripe webhook signature verification.
- Appropriate CSRF protection for the selected authentication design.
- Protection against unauthorized access to user resumes, chats, bookings, and profiles.

Do not expose internal stack traces in production responses.

Do not log passwords, secret keys, payment credentials, or unnecessary personal information.

Never commit real credentials to Git.

==================================================
24. ERROR HANDLING AND RELIABILITY
==================================================

Handle failures in all external integrations.

LLM failures:
- Timeouts.
- Rate limits.
- Invalid responses.
- Provider errors.

Stripe failures:
- Checkout creation errors.
- Failed payments.
- Invalid webhook signatures.
- Duplicate webhook delivery.

Calendar failures:
- Authentication errors.
- API timeouts.
- Duplicate event prevention.
- Retryable failures.

Email failures:
- Provider outages.
- Invalid recipient addresses.
- Temporary delivery errors.

Return understandable messages to the frontend.

Log technical details securely on the backend.

Where asynchronous retry is required, use a durable job mechanism if practical. Do not assume that an in-memory queue survives a server restart.

Do not add Redis or a message broker unless the basic implementation is working and the added complexity is justified.

==================================================
25. FRONTEND ROUTES
==================================================

Create the following pages using Next.js App Router:

PUBLIC:
- /
- /register
- /login

AUTHENTICATED:
- /dashboard
- /profile
- /chat
- /chat/[sessionId]
- /resumes
- /resumes/create
- /resumes/[id]/edit
- /resumes/[id]/preview
- /consultations
- /consultations/book

PAYMENT:
- /payment/success
- /payment/cancel

The payment-success page should display payment or booking status based on verified backend information. It must not independently confirm a payment.

Every page must be connected to the backend.

Implement loading, empty, success, and error states.

Ensure that navigation works correctly and that unauthorized users cannot access protected resources.

==================================================
26. AUTOMATED TESTING
==================================================

Create meaningful automated tests.

Minimum required backend coverage:

1. Authentication flow.
2. Resume creation and update.
3. Chat/session behavior.
4. Booking behavior.
5. Stripe webhook behavior.

Also test important edge cases.

Examples:
- Invalid login.
- Unauthorized access.
- Accessing another user's resume.
- Missing required resume fields.
- Invalid chat session.
- LLM timeout.
- Booking in the past.
- Double booking.
- Invalid booking state transition.
- Invalid Stripe webhook signature.
- Duplicate webhook delivery.
- Calendar API failure after successful payment.
- Email provider failure.

Use mocks or test adapters for external services when appropriate.

Tests must not require real payment transactions or send real emails.

Use isolated test data and a suitable test database configuration.

Run the tests and fix failures.

Do not claim that tests passed unless they were actually executed successfully.

==================================================
27. DOCUMENTATION
==================================================

Create a comprehensive README.md.

Include:

1. Project overview.
2. Feature list.
3. Technology stack.
4. Architecture diagram.
5. Module boundaries and reasoning.
6. Database schema overview.
7. Authentication strategy.
8. AI integration architecture.
9. Resume generation workflow.
10. Template rendering approach.
11. Payment workflow.
12. Webhook idempotency.
13. Calendar integration.
14. Email integration.
15. Environment variables.
16. Local setup instructions.
17. Frontend startup commands.
18. Backend startup commands.
19. MongoDB setup.
20. Stripe test setup.
21. Google Calendar setup.
22. LLM provider setup.
23. Email provider setup.
24. API documentation.
25. Testing instructions.
26. Docker instructions, if implemented.
27. Known limitations.
28. Technical trade-offs.
29. Scaling considerations for one million users.

Create a .env.example file with placeholder values.

Never place real credentials in the README.

==================================================
28. ENVIRONMENT CONFIGURATION
==================================================

Create a documented .env.example.

Include only variables actually used by the application.

Potential variables include:

NODE_ENV=
PORT=
FRONTEND_URL=
BACKEND_URL=
MONGODB_URI=
SESSION_SECRET=
JWT_SECRET=
LLM_PROVIDER=
LLM_API_KEY=
LLM_MODEL=
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=
NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=
GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI=
EMAIL_HOST=
EMAIL_PORT=
EMAIL_USER=
EMAIL_PASSWORD=
EMAIL_FROM=

Adjust these variables according to the actual implementation.

Do not expose server-only secrets through NEXT_PUBLIC variables.

Validate required environment variables at startup.

If optional external credentials are absent, show a clear setup warning and use mock adapters only where safe and appropriate.

Do not silently replace production functionality with fake success responses.

==================================================
29. OPTIONAL ENHANCEMENTS
==================================================

Implement these only after the mandatory functionality is working:

- Redis caching.
- AI streaming.
- Token usage tracking.
- Resume version history.
- Autosave.
- Resume duplication.
- Refresh-token rotation.
- Password reset.
- Email verification.
- End-to-end tests.
- Docker Compose.
- Structured observability.
- Durable asynchronous jobs.
- Advanced retry mechanisms.

Do not sacrifice mandatory functionality to implement bonuses.

==================================================
30. DEVELOPMENT WORKFLOW
==================================================

Follow this implementation process.

PHASE 1: WORKSPACE INSPECTION AND PLANNING

1. Inspect the current workspace.
2. Check existing files before modifying them.
3. Identify installed tools and available runtime versions.
4. Create an implementation checklist.
5. Design the architecture.
6. Create the project structure.
7. Document the required environment variables.
8. Identify integrations that require credentials.

Do not delete unrelated files.

PHASE 2: PROJECT FOUNDATION

1. Set up the frontend.
2. Set up the backend.
3. Configure TypeScript.

# Architecture Design Document

## 1. Executive Overview

The **AI-Powered Career and Consultation Platform** is engineered as a modern, high-performance, modular monolith. It bridges AI-assisted professional resume authoring, dynamic ChatGPT-style career coaching, and end-to-end consultant booking with verified Stripe payments and automated calendar/email orchestration.

## 2. High-Level Architecture Diagram

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                              Next.js 14+ Frontend (App Router)                    |
|  - Tailwind CSS + UI Design System                                                |
|  - Tiptap Rich Text Editor                                                        |
|  - Real-time Client State & React Hook Form + Zod Validation                      |
+-----------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+
                                          |
                                    REST / JSON
                                    HTTP-Only Cookies / Bearer Token
                                          v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                              Express.js Backend API Layer                         |
|  - Centralized Error Handling Middleware                                          |
|  - Role-Based Access Control (RBAC: USER, ADMIN, CONSULTANT)                      |
|  - Strict Zod Request Validation                                                  |
|  - Swagger / OpenAPI Auto-Documentation                                           |
+-----+--------------+---------------+--------------+---------------+---------------+
      |              |               |              |               |               |
      v              v               v              v               v               v
  [Auth & User]   [AI Chat]     [Resume & AI]  [Consultant]    [Booking]      [Payments]
  - Argon2/bcrypt - Persistent   - Structured   - Profiles     - Concurrency   - Stripe Session
  - Profile Mgmt  - Context LLM  - Tiptap Sync  - Availability - State Machine - Webhook Idemp.
      |              |               |              |               |               |
      +--------------+---------------+--------------+---------------+---------------+
                                          |
                                          v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                  MongoDB Database                                 |
|  - Indexed Schemas (Users, Resumes, ChatSessions, Bookings, Payments, etc.)       |
|  - Atomicity, Unique Compound Constraints & Isolated Multi-Tenant Scopes          |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                          |
                        +-----------------+-----------------+
                        | External Integration Adapters     |
                        +-----------------+-----------------+
                                          |
           +------------------------------+------------------------------+
           |                              |                              |
           v                              v                              v
     [LLM Providers]                [Stripe API]              [Google & Email]
  - OpenAI / Gemini               - Checkout Sessions       - Google Calendar v3
  - Standard Mock Adapter         - Webhooks (HMAC SHA256)  - Nodemailer / SMTP
```

## 3. Module Boundaries & Responsibilities

1. **Auth & User Management (`/modules/auth`, `/modules/users`)**:
   - Secure credential verification, password hashing with bcrypt/argon2.
   - JWT issuance via HTTP-Only cookies or authorization headers.
   - Profile management with skills, experience, education, headline, and bio.

2. **AI Career Assistant (`/modules/chat`)**:
   - Manages persistent chat sessions and chat messages.
   - Pluggable AI integration layer supporting OpenAI, Gemini, and Local Mock Adapter with realistic conversational capabilities.
   - Enforces ownership checks and session sanitization.

3. **Resume Management & AI Generation (`/modules/resumes`)**:
   - Stores structured resume entities (Personal Info, Summary, Experience, Education, Skills, Projects, Certifications, Achievements).
   - Generates and refines specific sections using structured LLM prompts.
   - Synchronizes with Tiptap rich-text editor without schema destruction.
   - Supports dual templates: **Modern Professional** and **ATS Classic** (semantic, clean, machine-parsable).

4. **Consultant & Booking Management (`/modules/consultants`, `/modules/bookings`)**:
   - Consultant directory with rates, expertise, bio, and time-slot availability.
   - Concurrency-safe booking engine preventing double-booking via MongoDB unique reservations and status validations.
   - Explicit Booking State Machine: `PENDING_PAYMENT`, `PAYMENT_FAILED`, `PAID`, `CONFIRMED`, `CANCELLED`, `COMPLETED`.

5. **Payment Processing (`/modules/payments`)**:
   - Stripe Checkout session creation with strictly server-calculated prices.
   - Cryptographic Stripe webhook signature verification (`stripe-signature`).
   - Idempotent event ledger ensuring duplicate webhooks never double-confirm or double-charge.

6. **External Integrations (`/integrations`)**:
   - **Google Calendar Adapter**: Creates events with meeting links upon booking confirmation. Gracefully handles external API outages with retryable markers without failing payments.
   - **Email Notification Adapter**: Dispatches formatted HTML confirmation emails with meeting links, agendas, and booking IDs via Nodemailer (with Mock fallback for local zero-config runs).

7. **Dashboard & Analytics (`/modules/dashboard`)**:
   - Server-side MongoDB aggregation pipeline returning user-scoped metrics: total resumes, active chats, upcoming consultations, and completed sessions.

8. **Listing Pagination, Search, Filtering (`/modules/bookings`, `/modules/consultants`)**:
   - Server-side pagination (`page`, `limit`), case-insensitive regex search, field sorting whitelist, and status filtering.

## 4. Key Design Decisions

- **Modular Monolith**: Eliminates network latency, distributed transaction complexity, and excessive container overhead while preserving clear interface boundaries.
- **Provider Adapters**: External services (LLM, Stripe, Google Calendar, SMTP) adhere to strict TypeScript interfaces. If API keys are absent, the system seamlessly uses self-contained development adapters that log actionable instructions without halting functionality.
- **Storage Independence**: Resume data is stored as a rich, structured schema (JSON) rather than unconstrained raw HTML, ensuring that template switching is lossless and deterministic.

# Database Design & Schemas

## 1. Overview

The platform uses **MongoDB** with **Mongoose ODM**. The schema balances document embedding for atomic sub-entities (e.g. resume work experiences, profile education items) with normalized references for entities possessing independent lifecycles (users, bookings, payments, consultants).

---

## 2. Collections & Schemas

### 2.1 Users (`users`)
- `_id`: ObjectId
- `name`: String (required, trimmed)
- `email`: String (required, unique, lowercase, indexed)
- `password`: String (required, bcrypt/argon2 hash)
- `role`: Enum `['USER', 'ADMIN', 'CONSULTANT']` (default: `'USER'`)
- `profile`: Embedded Document:
  - `phone`: String
  - `headline`: String
  - `bio`: String
  - `education`: Array of `{ school, degree, fieldOfStudy, startDate, endDate, description }`
  - `skills`: Array of String
  - `experience`: Array of `{ company, title, location, startDate, endDate, current, description }`
  - `projects`: Array of `{ title, link, description }`
  - `certifications`: Array of `{ name, issuer, issueDate }`
- `createdAt`: Date
- `updatedAt`: Date

**Indexes:**
- `{ email: 1 }` (unique)
- `{ role: 1 }`

---

### 2.2 Chat Sessions (`chatsessions`)
- `_id`: ObjectId
- `userId`: ObjectId (ref: `'User'`, required, indexed)
- `title`: String (default: `'New Career Conversation'`)
- `createdAt`: Date
- `updatedAt`: Date

**Indexes:**
- `{ userId: 1, updatedAt: -1 }`

---

### 2.3 Chat Messages (`chatmessages`)
- `_id`: ObjectId
- `sessionId`: ObjectId (ref: `'ChatSession'`, required, indexed)
- `userId`: ObjectId (ref: `'User'`, required, indexed)
- `role`: Enum `['user', 'assistant', 'system']`
- `content`: String (required)
- `createdAt`: Date

**Indexes:**
- `{ sessionId: 1, createdAt: 1 }`

---

### 2.4 Resumes (`resumes`)
- `_id`: ObjectId
- `userId`: ObjectId (ref: `'User'`, required, indexed)
- `title`: String (required, default: `'Untitled Resume'`)
- `template`: Enum `['MODERN_PROFESSIONAL', 'ATS_CLASSIC']` (default: `'MODERN_PROFESSIONAL'`)
- `personalInfo`:
  - `fullName`: String
  - `email`: String
  - `phone`: String
  - `location`: String
  - `linkedin`: String
  - `website`: String
- `summary`: String
- `experience`: Array of `{ id, company, role, location, startDate, endDate, current, description, highlights: [String] }`
- `education`: Array of `{ id, institution, degree, fieldOfStudy, startDate, endDate, gpa }`
- `skills`: Array of String
- `projects`: Array of `{ id, title, description, technologies: [String], link }`
- `certifications`: Array of `{ id, name, issuer, issueDate }`
- `achievements`: Array of String
- `customSections`: Array of `{ id, title, content }`
- `createdAt`: Date
- `updatedAt`: Date

**Indexes:**
- `{ userId: 1, updatedAt: -1 }`

---

### 2.5 Consultants (`consultants`)
- `_id`: ObjectId
- `name`: String (required)
- `title`: String (required)
- `bio`: String (required)
- `expertise`: Array of String
- `email`: String (required)
- `hourlyRate`: Number (in cents, e.g. 10000 = $100.00)
- `durationMinutes`: Number (default: 45)
- `isActive`: Boolean (default: true)
- `availability`: Array of `{ dayOfWeek: Number (0-6), startTime: String ("09:00"), endTime: String ("17:00") }`
- `createdAt`: Date
- `updatedAt`: Date

**Indexes:**
- `{ isActive: 1 }`
- `{ expertise: 1 }`

---

### 2.6 Bookings (`bookings`)
- `_id`: ObjectId
- `userId`: ObjectId (ref: `'User'`, required, indexed)
- `consultantId`: ObjectId (ref: `'Consultant'`, required, indexed)
- `userName`: String (required)
- `userEmail`: String (required)
- `userPhone`: String

# Testing Strategy & Test Plan

## 1. Overview

Testing covers critical backend APIs, authentication boundaries, concurrency constraints in appointment booking, and webhook idempotency.

---

## 2. Test Suites

### 2.1 Authentication & Profile (`tests/auth.test.ts`)
- Registration with valid data.
- Rejection of duplicate email addresses.
- Login with correct password vs incorrect password.
- JWT verification and rejection of unauthenticated requests to protected endpoints.
- User profile retrieval and updating.

### 2.2 Resume Management & AI Generation (`tests/resumes.test.ts`)
- Resume creation, listing, updating, and deletion.
- Access control: user A cannot read or modify user B's resume.
- Switching between `MODERN_PROFESSIONAL` and `ATS_CLASSIC` templates preserves structured data.
- AI resume generation endpoint with mock provider fallback.
- Export endpoint generating clean, semantic ATS-friendly markup.

### 2.3 AI Career Assistant (`tests/chat.test.ts`)
- Chat session creation, listing, updating (rename), and deletion.
- Sending messages, saving user message, and generating AI assistant reply.
- Multi-turn context preservation.
- Error handling and isolation across different users.

### 2.4 Consultation Booking & Concurrency (`tests/bookings.test.ts`)
- Rejecting bookings in the past.
- Validating consultant availability against active slots.
- Creating booking with status `PENDING_PAYMENT`.
- Concurrency test: preventing double-booking of identical slot.
- Server-side pagination, search, sorting, and filtering tests (`page`, `limit`, `status`, `search`).

### 2.5 Payments, Stripe Webhooks & Idempotency (`tests/payments.test.ts`)
- Creating checkout session with server-calculated pricing.
- Verifying invalid Stripe webhook signature is rejected with HTTP 400.
- Processing valid `checkout.session.completed` event: transitions booking to `CONFIRMED` and payment to `SUCCEEDED`.
- Duplicate webhook test: re-sending the same webhook event ID does not duplicate records or cause state regression.
- Graceful handling of calendar and email integration failures without rolling back confirmed payments.

---

## 3. Test Database Environment
Backend tests execute with `mongodb-memory-server` or an isolated temporary MongoDB test instance to ensure zero mutation of production or local development data.

# CareerOS: AI-Powered Career and Consultation Platform

An enterprise-grade, full-stack career platform featuring an **interactive ChatGPT-style AI career assistant**, a **structured multi-template AI resume builder with Tiptap editor**, and **verified 1-on-1 expert consultation bookings with Stripe payment integration, Google Calendar synchronization, and automated email confirmations**.

---

## 1. Project Overview

CareerOS bridges advanced generative AI capabilities with real-world professional coaching workflows:
1. **Secure Multi-Role Authentication**: JWT stored in HTTP-Only cookies with Argon2/bcrypt password hashing and role-based access control (`USER`, `ADMIN`, `CONSULTANT`).
2. **AI Career Assistant**: ChatGPT-style persistent coaching conversations supporting the STAR behavioral method, system design prep, and offer negotiation.
3. **Structured AI Resume Builder**: Lossless structured resume authoring with Tiptap rich-text formatting and live switching between **Modern Professional** and **ATS Classic** templates.
4. **ATS Machine-Readable Output**: Semantic HTML hierarchy for high parseability, keyword extraction, and instant export/PDF printing.
5. **Concurrency-Guarded Consultation Engine**: Prevents double-bookings and past bookings with compound database constraints.
6. **Stripe Payments with Webhook Idempotency**: Server-side pricing enforcement, cryptographic HMAC signature validation, and event ledger idempotency.
7. **Calendar & Email Orchestration**: Automated Google Meet link creation and Nodemailer email delivery, designed with graceful failure isolation (payment success is preserved even if third-party APIs encounter outages).
8. **Real-time Analytics Dashboard**: Server-side MongoDB aggregation pipeline returning user-scoped resume metrics, active chat sessions, and upcoming consultations.

---

## 2. Technology Stack

### Frontend
- **Framework**: Next.js 14+ (App Router, Server & Client Components)
- **Language**: TypeScript (Strict mode)
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS
- **Rich Text Editor**: Tiptap (`@tiptap/react`, `@tiptap/starter-kit`)
- **Forms & Validation**: React Hook Form with Zod schemas
- **Icons**: Lucide React

### Backend
- **Runtime**: Node.js v20+ / v22+
- **Server Framework**: Express.js with TypeScript
- **Database ODM**: Mongoose with MongoDB
- **Security**: Helmet, CORS with credentials, cookie-parser, bcryptjs
- **Validation**: Zod (request body, query, and params validation)
- **Logging**: Structured logger with severity levels (`info`, `warn`, `error`, `debug`)
- **API Documentation**: OpenAPI / Swagger UI (`/api/docs`)

### Testing
- **Test Runner**: Jest (`ts-jest`)
- **API Testing**: Supertest
- **Database Test Isolation**: In-memory MongoDB (`mongodb-memory-server`)

---

## 3. Architecture & System Flow

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                              Next.js 14+ Frontend (App Router)                    |
|  - Tailwind CSS + UI Design System                                                |
|  - Tiptap Rich Text Editor                                                        |
|  - Real-time Client State & React Hook Form + Zod Validation                      |
+-----------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+
                                          |
                                    REST / JSON
                                    HTTP-Only Cookies / Bearer Token
                                          v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                              Express.js Backend API Layer                         |
|  - Centralized Error Handling Middleware                                          |
|  - Role-Based Access Control (RBAC: USER, ADMIN, CONSULTANT)                      |
|  - Strict Zod Request Validation                                                  |
|  - Swagger / OpenAPI Auto-Documentation                                           |
+-----+--------------+---------------+--------------+---------------+---------------+
      |              |               |              |               |               |
      v              v               v              v               v               v
  [Auth & User]   [AI Chat]     [Resume & AI]  [Consultant]    [Booking]      [Payments]
  - Argon2/bcrypt - Persistent   - Structured   - Profiles     - Concurrency   - Stripe Session
  - Profile Mgmt  - Context LLM  - Tiptap Sync  - Availability - State Machine - Webhook Idemp.
      |              |               |              |               |               |
      +--------------+---------------+--------------+---------------+---------------+
                                          |
                                          v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                  MongoDB Database                                 |
|  - Indexed Schemas (Users, Resumes, ChatSessions, Bookings, Payments, etc.)       |
|  - Atomicity, Unique Compound Constraints & Isolated Multi-Tenant Scopes          |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                          |
                        +-----------------+-----------------+
                        | External Integration Adapters     |
                        +-----------------+-----------------+
                                          |
           +------------------------------+------------------------------+
           |                              |                              |
           v                              v                              v
     [LLM Providers]                [Stripe API]              [Google & Email]
  - OpenAI / Gemini               - Checkout Sessions       - Google Calendar v3
  - Standard Mock Adapter         - Webhooks (HMAC SHA256)  - Nodemailer / SMTP
```

---

## 4. Module Boundaries & Design Rationale

1. **Auth & User (`/modules/auth`, `/modules/users`)**: Encapsulates credential management and profiles. Passwords are never returned in queries.
2. **AI Chat (`/modules/chat`)**: Manages session metadata and message threads. LLM calls run server-side only; keys are never sent to the browser.
3. **Resumes (`/modules/resumes`)**: Stores raw data in structured JSON schemas rather than unstructured HTML. This allows lossless template switching.
4. **Consultants & Bookings (`/modules/consultants`, `/modules/bookings`)**: Implements strict overlapping verification and past-date rejection.
5. **Payments (`/modules/payments`)**: Adheres to strict server-side pricing. The client cannot forge or alter the checkout price.
6. **External Integrations (`/integrations`)**: Abstracted via adapters (`llm.ts`, `calendar.ts`, `email.ts`). If external API credentials are not provided, built-in development fallback adapters maintain zero-friction local functionality.

---

## 5. Database Schema Overview

- **User**: Name, unique lowercase email, bcrypt password hash, role (`USER`, `ADMIN`, `CONSULTANT`), embedded profile (headline, bio, skills, education, experience, projects).
- **ChatSession**: User reference, title, timestamps, compound index on `{ userId: 1, updatedAt: -1 }`.
- **ChatMessage**: Session reference, user reference, role (`user`, `assistant`, `system`), content, indexed by session and creation time.
- **Resume**: User reference, title, template (`MODERN_PROFESSIONAL` or `ATS_CLASSIC`), structured personal info, summary, experience, education, skills, projects, certifications, achievements.
- **Consultant**: Name, title, bio, expertise array, hourly rate (cents), session duration, availability array (day of week, start/end time), active status.
- **Booking**: User reference, consultant reference, agenda, start time, end time, duration, server-calculated amount, status state machine (`PENDING_PAYMENT`, `PAYMENT_FAILED`, `PAID`, `CONFIRMED`, `CANCELLED`, `COMPLETED`), calendar & email integration status.
- **Payment**: Booking reference (unique), user reference, Stripe session ID (unique), payment intent ID, amount, currency, status (`PENDING`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`), processed webhook events array (for strict idempotency).

---

## 6. Authentication Strategy

- **Tokens**: JSON Web Tokens (JWT) signed with HMAC SHA-256.
- **Cookie Security**: Issued in `HTTP-Only`, `SameSite: Lax`, and `Secure` (in production) cookies to prevent XSS credential theft.
- **Authorization Header**: Bearer token is supported as a fallback for API clients and automated tests.
- **Access Isolation**: Every database query filters by `userId: req.user.userId`. Cross-user data access is rejected with `HTTP 403 Forbidden`.

---

## 7. AI Resume Generation & Templates

### Two Production Templates:
1. **Modern Professional**: Modern typography (Inter), clear visual hierarchy, balanced whitespace, modern header, clean badge styling.
2. **ATS Classic**: Traditional serif typography (Times New Roman), standardized single-column layout, semantic heading hierarchy, machine-readable formatting designed for applicant tracking systems.

Both templates consume the same underlying JSON data model. Switching templates in the editor or preview changes only presentation; no resume fields are lost or duplicated.

---

## 8. Stripe Payment Workflow & Webhook Idempotency

1. User selects an open slot for an expert.
2. Backend checks availability, calculates the price, and creates a `PENDING_PAYMENT` booking.
3. User initiates checkout -> backend creates a Stripe Checkout Session with line items calculated strictly from the database.
4. User completes payment on Stripe.
5. Stripe sends `checkout.session.completed` webhook to `/api/payments/webhook`.
6. Backend verifies the raw HMAC signature using `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent()`.
7. **Idempotency check**: The backend inspects `Payment.processedWebhookEvents`. If the event ID was already recorded, the handler responds immediately with HTTP 200 without duplicate action.
8. Transition booking to `CONFIRMED` and payment to `SUCCEEDED`.
9. Trigger Google Calendar and Email invitations. If either fails, the booking remains confirmed and the error is logged without failing the payment.

---

## 9. Environment Variables

Create a `.env` file in the project root or backend folder:

```env
# Server
NODE_ENV=development
PORT=5000
FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost:3000
BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:5000

# Database
MONGODB_URI=mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/career_platform

# Security
JWT_SECRET=super-secret-jwt-key-min-32-chars-long-for-production-security
JWT_EXPIRES_IN=7d
COOKIE_SECRET=super-secret-cookie-secret-key-32-chars-long

# AI Provider ('mock', 'openai', 'gemini')
LLM_PROVIDER=mock
LLM_API_KEY=
LLM_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini

# Stripe Payments
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_placeholder_key
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_placeholder_webhook_secret
NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_test_placeholder_publishable_key

# Google Calendar (optional, uses MockAdapter if empty)
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=
GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:5000/api/calendar/callback
GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN=

# Email SMTP (optional, uses MockAdapter if empty)
EMAIL_HOST=smtp.mailtrap.io
EMAIL_PORT=587
EMAIL_USER=
EMAIL_PASSWORD=
EMAIL_FROM=no-reply@careerplatform.com
```

---

## 10. Local Setup & Startup Instructions

### Prerequisites
- Node.js v20+ or v22+
- npm v10+
- MongoDB (local `mongod` or Docker container)

### 1. Start MongoDB
Using the installed MongoDB server:
```powershell
mongod --dbpath ./data/db
```
Or via Docker:
```bash
docker compose up -d mongodb
```

### 2. Backend Setup & Run
```bash
cd backend
npm install
npm run dev
```
Backend will start on `http://localhost:5000`.
- Swagger API Docs: `http://localhost:5000/api/docs`
- Health check: `http://localhost:5000/health`

### 3. Frontend Setup & Run
```bash
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```
Frontend will be accessible at `http://localhost:3000`.

---

## 11. Automated Testing

All 5 core suites run against an isolated in-memory MongoDB instance:

```bash
cd backend
npm test
```

### Test Coverage Summary:
- **Authentication**: Registration, duplicate email rejection, password checks, HTTP-only cookie issuance, profile update.
- **Resumes**: CRUD, user access isolation, template switching, AI generation, semantic export.
- **AI Chat Assistant**: Multi-turn message exchange, history retention, session rename, deletion, access isolation.
- **Consultation Booking**: Past booking rejection, slot reservation, concurrency conflict (double-booking) rejection, server-side pagination, search, and filtering.
- **Stripe Payments**: Server pricing, webhook processing, state transition to `CONFIRMED`, webhook idempotency, integration failure isolation.

---

## 12. Production Build

Build backend:
```bash
cd backend
npm run build
```

Build frontend:
```bash
cd frontend
npm run build
```

---

## 13. Scaling Considerations for 1 Million Users

1. **Stateless Backend**: Express APIs are stateless; horizontal autoscaling behind AWS ALB or Cloudflare.
2. **MongoDB Sharding**: Shard `chatmessages` by `{ sessionId: 1 }` and `resumes` by `{ userId: 1 }`.
3. **Read Replicas**: Route dashboard queries and consultant availability searches to secondary replicas.
4. **Redis Cache Layer**: Cache consultant availability slots and public consultant directory with TTL invalidation.
5. **Durable Message Queues**: Queue Stripe webhook jobs and email/calendar dispatches via RabbitMQ or AWS SQS.

# AI-Powered Career and Consultation Platform

The **CareerOS Platform** has been fully implemented, tested, and built. It is a complete, production-oriented full-stack web application with Next.js 14 App Router on the frontend, Express.js with TypeScript and Mongoose on the backend, persistent MongoDB database schemas, LLM integration, Stripe Checkout with webhook idempotency, Google Calendar synchronization, automated email confirmations, and automated test coverage.

The project is located at:

> [!NOTE]
> It is recommended to set `C:\Users\PRIYANKA\.gemini\antigravity\scratch\career-platform` as your active workspace directory in your editor or terminal.

---

## 1. Summary of Implemented Features

### 1. Authentication & User Profile Management
- Secure user registration and login with bcrypt password hashing.
- Token-based authentication using JSON Web Tokens (JWT) issued in **HTTP-Only cookies** (`token`) with Bearer header fallback.
- Role-based authorization (`USER`, `ADMIN`, `CONSULTANT`).
- Comprehensive profile management: Headline, biography, contact info, skills, education, work experience, projects, and certifications.
- Protected frontend routes and backend APIs with resource ownership verification.

### 2. AI Career Assistant (ChatGPT-Style Coach)
- Persistent multi-turn conversations stored in MongoDB ([`ChatSession`](file:///C:/Users/PRIYANKA/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/career-platform/backend/src/modules/chat/chat.model.ts) and [`ChatMessage`](file:///C:/Users/PRIYANKA/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/career-platform/backend/src/modules/chat/chat.model.ts)).
- Real-time conversation context preservation (STAR interview method, salary negotiation strategies, system design coaching).
- Session management: Create new chats, rename sessions with inline modals, switch between threads, and delete sessions.
- Pluggable AI provider abstraction ([`llm.ts`](file:///C:/Users/PRIYANKA/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/career-platform/backend/src/integrations/llm.ts)) supporting OpenAI, Gemini, and a development fallback mock provider.

### 3. AI Resume Builder & Tiptap Rich Text Editor
- Multi-section structured resume model ([`Resume`](file:///C:/Users/PRIYANKA/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/career-platform/backend/src/modules/resumes/resume.model.ts)): Personal info, summary, experience, education, skills, projects, certifications, and achievements.
- Resume content stored independently of visual presentation (no destructive raw HTML coupling).
- Interactive **Tiptap rich text editor** ([`TiptapResumeEditor.tsx`](file:///C:/Users/PRIYANKA/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/career-platform/frontend/components/editor/TiptapResumeEditor.tsx)) supporting bold, italics, headers, and bulleted/numbered lists with bidirectional state synchronization.
- Targeted AI section generation/refinement: Users can trigger AI generation specifically for summary, experience bullets, or skills without altering other fields.
- Full CRUD operations: Create, list, edit, preview, delete, and export resumes.

### 4. Dual Resume Templates & ATS-Friendly Output
- **Template A: Modern Professional**: Contemporary typography, clear visual hierarchy, balanced whitespace, and subtle border accents.
- **Template B: ATS Classic**: Single-column conventional layout, semantic HTML heading hierarchy (`header`, `main`, `section`, `h1`, `h2`, `h3`, `ul`, `li`), and machine-readable text designed for applicant tracking systems.
- Seamless template switching: Switching templates updates presentation while preserving structured resume data.
- Export options: One-click browser print / PDF export (`window.print()`) and downloadable raw semantic HTML.

### 5. Consultant Directory & Concurrency-Guarded Booking
- Consultant directory with real-time slot availability calculation.
- Seeded demonstration experts: Sarah Jenkins (Staff Recruiter), David Chen (VP of Engineering), and Maya Patel (Design Director).
- Strict business validation: Rejection of bookings in the past, time-boundary validation, and active slot verification.
- **Concurrency & Overlapping Safeguards**: Database-level overlapping reservation query prevents double-booking identical or intersecting slots (returns `HTTP 409 Conflict`).
- Explicit booking state machine: `PENDING_PAYMENT` $\rightarrow$ `PAID` $\rightarrow$ `CONFIRMED`, `PAYMENT_FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `COMPLETED`.

### 6. Stripe Payment Integration & Webhook Idempotency
- Server-side price calculation: The browser cannot specify or forge consultation fees.
- Stripe Checkout session creation (`/api/payments/checkout`) with automatic redirects.
- Webhook signature verification: Cryptographic HMAC SHA256 verification using `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent()`.
- **Event Ledger Idempotency**: Processed Stripe event IDs (`event.id`) are tracked in [`Payment.processedWebhookEvents`](file:///C:/Users/PRIYANKA/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/career-platform/backend/src/modules/payments/payment.model.ts). Re-delivering identical webhook events returns `HTTP 200` without duplicating state transitions or notifications.
- Verified payment status page (`/payment/success`) validates payment and booking status via backend database verification rather than trusting browser redirects.

### 7. Google Calendar & Email Integrations with Failure Isolation
- **Google Calendar Adapter** ([`calendar.ts`](file:///C:/Users/PRIYANKA/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/career-platform/backend/src/integrations/calendar.ts)): Generates meeting event IDs and Google Meet video links.
- **Email Adapter** ([`email.ts`](file:///C:/Users/PRIYANKA/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/career-platform/backend/src/integrations/email.ts)): Dispatches HTML confirmation emails containing the booking ID, date, time, consultant details, agenda, and video link.
- **Failure Isolation**: If Google Calendar or Nodemailer encounters third-party outages, the confirmed payment and booking status are preserved; integration errors are flagged on the booking record (`calendarStatus: 'FAILED'`, `emailStatus: 'FAILED'`) for asynchronous retries.

### 8. Analytics Dashboard & Server-Side Pagination
- User-scoped dashboard aggregation pipeline ([`dashboard.controller.ts`](file:///C:/Users/PRIYANKA/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/career-platform/backend/src/modules/dashboard/dashboard.controller.ts)): Total resumes, total chat sessions, upcoming consultations, completed consultations, recent resumes, and upcoming appointments.
- Server-side pagination, search, sorting whitelist, and status filtering on the consultations listing API ([`booking.controller.ts`](file:///C:/Users/PRIYANKA/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/career-platform/backend/src/modules/bookings/booking.controller.ts)).

## 9. Known Limitations & Technical Trade-offs

1. **In-Memory vs. Distributed Job Queue**: Stripe webhook delivery and subsequent calendar/email operations execute synchronously within the webhook transaction. In an ultra-high-throughput enterprise setup, scheduling calendar and email jobs through a durable queue (e.g. BullMQ / Redis) provides distributed worker retries across restarts.
2. **ATS Compatibility**: The ATS Classic template conforms to semantic HTML, standard section hierarchies, single-column design, and raw text readability. However, because enterprise applicant tracking parsers vary widely across vendors (Workday, Taleo, Greenhouse, Lever), universal 100% parsing fidelity cannot be mathematically guaranteed across all proprietary engines.
3. **Local Development Adapters**: When API keys are not supplied for OpenAI, Stripe, Google Calendar, or Nodemailer, development adapters return deterministic mock data with explicit log markers.
